public_rationale: The evidence supports the existence of accessible, inexpensive synthetic-media tools by February 2026. It does not settle the stronger combination Marcus asserts: convincing video impersonation of arbitrary people, on demand, for almost nothing. Free access or selected demonstrations alone would not establish that combination. The gaps also do not justify calling it false.
limitations: The scientific synthesis is broader than person-specific video impersonation.
The Seedance publication is retrospective and supplies no February cost measurements.
A narrower reading limited to some people and some low-cost clips would be easier to support.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Given sufficient data, deepfake tools can now fake anybody's appearance at any time for almost no cost.

statement.excerpt: Anybody’s appearance can (given sufficient data) be faked now, at any time, for almost nothing.
statement.document_title: We URGENTLY need a federal law forbidding AI from impersonating humans

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that available tools can produce convincing short videos depicting arbitrary people, given adequate source imagery, on demand and at negligible production cost.
This does not require flawless impersonation in every scene or fooling every viewer.
Because 'now' describes an ongoing capability without a reporting period, the target is February 2026 through the post date.
Free software alone does not establish negligible production cost; hardware, processing, preparation and retries also matter.
criteria.support_condition: Dated demonstrations or evaluations establish broad identity coverage, convincing video likenesses and negligible production costs using tools available by February 14, 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evaluations establish substantial identity, availability or cost barriers that defeat this ordinary reading even with sufficient source data.
